q-3857: Correct answer: B. In a vehicle without ABS, braking too hard locks the wheels; locked wheels do not steer the vehicle, so the steering stops working and the car slides on in its current direction. You must then release the pedal for a moment and brake again.
q-3858: Correct answer: B. In a vehicle with ABS the brake pedal is pressed quickly and hard, and the system itself pulses the braking force so that the wheels do not lock. Braking interrupted by the driver only lengthens the stopping distance.
q-3859: Correct answer: A. Pulsing of the pedal is a normal sign that ABS is working, not a fault, so the pressure must be kept up until the vehicle stops or the danger passes. Easing off or releasing the pedal interrupts the braking and lengthens the stopping distance.
q-3860: Correct answer: A. ABS does not let the wheels lock, so even while braking in a sideways skid the wheels still respond to the steering and the vehicle can be steered. It works the same on a straight and in a bend, but it is no substitute for careful driving.
q-3882: Correct answer: B. A red brake-system warning light signals a fault that threatens braking performance, so you must stop the vehicle in a safe place and check the brake fluid level. Driving on with faulty brakes is not permitted.
q-3885: Correct answer: A. A red cooling-system warning light warns that the coolant temperature is too high. Driving on risks serious engine damage, so stop the vehicle in a safe place and let the engine cool down.
q-3891: Correct answer: C. A space-saver spare is intended precisely for a damaged tyre and may be used briefly, at the speed marked on the wheel. Worn brakes and damaged shock absorbers directly impair braking and stability, so they rule out driving.
q-4479: Correct answer: C. The light with the battery symbol signals that the charging system is not supplying current, so the vehicle is running solely on the energy stored in the battery. Shorten the journey to the nearest workshop and switch off unnecessary electrical consumers.
q-4481: Correct answer: A. A lit oil-pressure light means that oil is not reaching the engine's moving parts at the correct pressure. Driving on leads to overheating and seizure, so stop the vehicle safely and switch off the engine.
q-4483: Correct answer: B. The driver of a vehicle fitted with seat belts must use them for the whole journey. Exempt from the duty are, among others, women who are visibly pregnant and people carried in a wheelchair.
q-4485: Correct answer: A. The belt holds the body against the seat, spreads the force of the impact over strong parts of the skeleton and prevents striking the interior or being thrown out of the vehicle. As a result the risk of serious and fatal injuries falls clearly.
q-4495: Correct answer: A. ABS does not let the wheels lock under braking, so the vehicle stays stable and steerable and the driver can steer round an obstacle. The system does not change the laws of physics, though, and does not protect against the effects of excessive speed.
q-4593: Correct answer: C. A red oil-pressure light means there is no proper lubrication, and keeping the engine running risks seizing it in a very short time. Pull over safely, stop the vehicle and switch off the engine immediately, and only then check the oil level.
q-6337: Correct answer: C. ABS does not let the wheels lock under braking, so the vehicle stays steerable and the driver can steer round an obstacle without easing off the brake. It does not shorten the braking distance in all conditions: on gravel or fresh snow it can even be longer.
q-6338: Correct answer: C. In a vehicle with ABS you brake by pressing the pedal fully and keeping up the pressure, because the system itself modulates the braking force wheel by wheel. Pumping the pedal or pressing gently only lengthens the braking distance.
q-6339: Correct answer: A. ABS keeps the wheels turning during braking, so the steering stays effective and you can change course. It does not shorten the braking distance in all conditions, and grip of the driven wheels under acceleration is the job of traction control.
q-6340: Correct answer: C. An airbag is a supplement to the seat belt: it cushions the body's impact and reduces injuries to the driver and passengers. It gives no complete protection and does not protect the bodywork, and with the belt unfastened it can itself cause injury.
q-6344: Correct answer: B. The duty to use seat belts always applies when driving on a road, regardless of speed, length of journey and conditions. Even at low speed the forces in a collision exceed what human muscles can hold many times over.
q-6368: Correct answer: B. The blind spot is a permanent feature of mirrors, but moving the head and torso shifts the field of view and lets you uncover it. That is why a dynamic posture is recommended, and before a lane change an additional look over the shoulder.
q-6371: Correct answer: C. The interior mirror serves to watch the road behind the vehicle and should take in the whole rear window. Aiming it at a child or at your own face deprives the driver of the picture of what is happening behind and makes it harder to judge the situation before a lane change or braking.
q-6372: Correct answer: B. The interior mirror is adjusted in the driving position, without lifting the back off the backrest, so that its frame takes in the whole rear window and the road behind the vehicle. Set this way it complements the picture from the exterior mirrors and reduces the blind spot.
q-6378: Correct answer: B. An exterior mirror should show the road behind the vehicle together with a narrow strip of your own side, which gives a reference point for judging distance. Set this way it also covers the neighbouring lane and reduces the blind spot.
q-6379: Correct answer: A. Emergency braking with ABS means pressing the pedal hard and keeping up the pressure until the vehicle stops; vibration and pulsing of the pedal mean the system is working. Easing off or pumping the brake interrupts its operation and lengthens the braking distance.
q-6388: Correct answer: C. The duty to fasten seat belts covers the driver and every passenger, in the front and in the back, in town and outside it. The exceptions are few and concern, among others, people with an appropriate medical certificate and children carried in child seats.
q-6393: Correct answer: A. The duty to fasten seat belts applies on all public roads, regardless of the type of surface and whether it is a built-up area. The type of road does not change the physics of a collision: even at low speed an unbelted body is thrown forward.
q-6407: Correct answer: C. The compulsory equipment of a car is a fire extinguisher and a reflective warning triangle. A first-aid kit and a spare wheel can be useful, but they are not required. The extinguisher must be easily accessible and have a valid inspection, otherwise it will be useless in a fire.
q-6410: Correct answer: B. Every car must have a reflective warning triangle and a fire extinguisher. A jack and a reflective vest are recommended but not compulsory. The triangle should be kept in an easily accessible place, because it serves to mark an immobilised vehicle.
q-6411: Correct answer: A. The compulsory equipment of a car includes a reflective warning triangle and a fire extinguisher. Spare bulbs and a hands-free kit can be useful, but the rules do not require them. The triangle marks a stopped vehicle so as to warn others early enough.
q-6412: Correct answer: A. A fire extinguisher, alongside a reflective warning triangle, is part of a car's compulsory equipment. Satellite navigation and a belt cutter can come in handy, but the rules do not require them. The extinguisher must be within the driver's reach and in working order.
q-6417: Correct answer: C. After losing a plate, the owner must apply to the office for a legalised duplicate; only a plate with the official legalisation mark is valid. Driving with one plate, or with a plate without legalisation, is not permitted.
q-6432: Correct answer: B. The seat belt keeps the driver's body in place and spreads the forces of a collision, so without it the risk of serious injuries grows — from striking the steering wheel, the windscreen or the interior. The belt has no effect on damage to the vehicle itself or on the airbag.
q-6438: Correct answer: C. Worn tread does not clear water from under the tyre, so grip falls and the braking distance grows; the risk of aquaplaning also increases. On a wet surface the effects are much stronger than on a dry one.
q-6440: Correct answer: C. An unbalanced wheel vibrates while driving and presses the tyre onto the road unevenly, which locally speeds up tread wear. Vibration at the steering wheel and faster wear of suspension parts are felt as well.
q-7441: Correct answer: C. A woman who is visibly pregnant is exempt from the duty to fasten seat belts. A place on the rear seat or eating a meal gives no such exemption — belts are compulsory in every seat fitted with them.
q-7457: Correct answer: C. Snow chains may be used only when the road is covered with snow. Neither the season nor a temperature below zero in itself entitles you to use them, because on a bare surface chains damage the road and worsen the vehicle's handling.
q-7463: Correct answer: B. ABS does not let the wheels lock under hard braking, so the vehicle stays steerable and you can steer round an obstacle. The braking distance is not always shorter — on loose snow or gravel it can even be longer.
q-7515: Correct answer: C. The number plate must be visible and legible at all times, so driving with a covered plate is prohibited. A protruding load is no excuse — it must be arranged so that the plate stays uncovered.
q-7517: Correct answer: C. A blue warning light on the dashboard always signals that main-beam headlights are on. Position lights and dipped headlights have green lights, so on noticing the blue one you must switch the lights so as not to dazzle other drivers.
q-7518: Correct answer: C. Clearly faster flashing of the indicator warning light is the typical signal of a blown bulb in one of the indicators. Check the indicators on both sides and replace the failed bulb, because other road users will not read your intended manoeuvre.
q-7709: Correct answer: C. A well-adjusted exterior mirror shows a narrow strip of your own vehicle's side as a reference point and the space behind the vehicle on that side. This setting reduces the blind spot, which must still be checked with a look over the shoulder.
q-7710: Correct answer: A. In a vehicle with ABS, emergency braking means pressing the brake pedal quickly and hard and keeping up the pressure — the system itself prevents the wheels from locking. Pumping the brake or increasing the pressure gradually only lengthens the braking distance.
q-8935: Correct answer: B. Abrasion, narrowing and tears in the webbing reduce its strength, so the belt may snap under load in a collision. Such a belt must be replaced with a new one; a twisted belt or stains are not in themselves a reason for replacement.
q-8993: Correct answer: C. The ABS system does not let the wheels lock under hard braking, so the vehicle stays steerable and you can steer round an obstacle. Cruise control only holds a set speed and does not help with braking.
q-9065: Correct answer: C. The ASR system works during acceleration: it detects spin of the driven wheels and limits drive torque, and a wet surface favours loss of grip. When descending a hill, slowing down is the job of the brakes and other systems.
q-9067: Correct answer: C. ASR is most useful when moving off sharply on a slippery surface, because the driven wheels then spin easily and the rear of the vehicle can swing out. The system then limits the drive and lets you move off smoothly.
q-9068: Correct answer: A. ESP compares the path set by the steering wheel with the vehicle's actual movement and brakes individual wheels when the car begins to run wide in a bend or to skid. It is precisely in a sharp bend that this correction is most needed.
q-9070: Correct answer: C. Through several bends in succession the body leans first one way and then the other, and the rear easily swings out. ESP then corrects the vehicle's path by braking selected wheels; at a steady speed there is nothing to stabilise.
q-9089: Correct answer: C. Dipped headlights are signalled by a green light with a headlamp symbol whose beam points diagonally downwards — that light is marked C in the material. A horizontal beam would mean main-beam headlights.
q-9090: Correct answer: A. An indicator in use is shown by a green flashing arrow pointing left or right — in the material that is light A. Both arrows flashing at once would mean the hazard lights.
q-9092: Correct answer: C. Position lights are signalled by a green light with a symbol of two lamps sending rays out to the sides — in the material it is marked C. Position lights alone are not enough for driving after dusk.
q-9093: Correct answer: B. Front fog lights have a green light with a lamp symbol whose straight rays are crossed by a wavy line — in the material that is light B. They may be used only in fog or precipitation, or dense fog limiting visibility.
q-9094: Correct answer: A. An indicator in use is shown by a green flashing arrow pointing left or right — in the material that is light A. Both arrows flashing at once would mean the hazard lights.
q-9095: Correct answer: A. Rear fog lights have an orange light with a lamp whose rays point backwards and are crossed by a wavy line — in the material that is light A. Once visibility improves they must be switched off, because they dazzle drivers behind.
q-9096: Correct answer: B. Main-beam headlights are signalled by a blue light with a headlamp and a horizontal, straight beam of rays — in the material that is light B. The blue colour is a reminder that they must be switched off for other road users.
q-9102: Correct answer: B. Unfastened seat belts are signalled by a red light with the silhouette of a seated person with a belt across them, often together with a sound — in the material that is light B. It goes out only once the belts are fastened.
q-9105: Correct answer: B. A red warning light means a fault that threatens safety or risks destroying the engine, so when it comes on you should stop the vehicle safely and remove the cause. In the material such a light is B; lights in other colours usually only inform.
q-9110: Correct answer: B. Rear-window heating is signalled by a light with a rectangle of the window and wavy arrows pointing upwards — in the material that is light B. It is a comfort function, not a fault warning; once the window has demisted it is worth switching off.
q-10048: Correct answer: B. The warning triangle serves to mark a vehicle immobilised on the road, for example after a breakdown, so that other drivers notice the obstacle early enough. It is placed behind the vehicle, and the required distance depends on the type of road.
q-10050: Correct answer: B. ABS is part of the braking system: sensors detect a wheel locking and automatically reduce the braking force on it. As a result the wheels keep turning and the driver retains the ability to steer the vehicle while braking.
q-10054: Correct answer: A. Without working ABS the wheels lock easily, and a vehicle with locked wheels loses steering. Pumping the brake, that is, alternately pressing and releasing the pedal, lets you slow down while keeping control of your course.
q-10072: Correct answer: C. An exterior mirror is set so that a small strip of the vehicle's side is visible at its inner edge, with the rest showing the road behind. Such a reference point makes it easier to judge distance and reduces the blind spot.
q-10102: Correct answer: B. With incorrect wheel alignment the wheels do not roll exactly in the direction of travel, so the tread constantly scrubs on the surface and wears quickly and unevenly. The characteristic symptom is wear mainly on the inner or the outer edge of the tyre.
q-10104: Correct answer: C. Bulges and deformations in the sidewall mean damage to the tyre's carcass; such a tyre can burst at speed at any moment and cannot be repaired. A damaged valve is replaced separately, and a puncture in the tread may be repaired professionally.
q-1864: Correct answer: A. A quadricycle other than a light one may be driven on a category B1 driving licence. Category AM covers a moped and a light quadricycle, and category A concerns motorcycles.
q-1866: Correct answer: A. The owner of a vehicle must have it undergo periodic technical inspections, because only a vehicle with a valid inspection may be used on the road. Personal accident insurance and comprehensive cover are voluntary.
q-3353: Correct answer: B. While driving you may not use a phone that requires holding the handset or microphone in the hand, because it occupies the driver's hand and attention. Carrying an intoxicated person and using cruise control in a built-up area are not prohibited.
q-4369: Correct answer: C. Alcohol disturbs the cooperation of the eyes and the brain: it lengthens reaction time, weakens the judgement of distance and narrows the field of vision to a thin slice ahead of the vehicle. A short rest or blinking does not have such an effect.
q-4370: Correct answer: A. A seat set too low hides the road behind the edge of the bonnet and the dashboard, and one set too high limits the view with the top edge of the windscreen. Correct seat adjustment is a condition of a full field of vision and easy operation of the vehicle.
q-6387: Correct answer: A. The number of seats, and thus the permitted number of people carried, is entered in the vehicle's registration document. The driving licence only specifies the categories of vehicle you may drive, and the insurance document concerns liability for damage caused.
q-6390: Correct answer: C. Using a phone while driving is prohibited if it requires holding the handset or microphone in the hand. Switching on the loudspeaker mode changes nothing, because the hand is occupied and attention divided. Only a kit that does not require holding the phone is allowed.
q-6391: Correct answer: B. Category B entitles you to drive a vehicle designed to carry no more than eight people besides the driver, that is, nine people including the driver. A vehicle with more seats requires a category D1 or D licence.
q-6401: Correct answer: A. Category B allows you to drive a vehicle with a maximum permissible mass of up to 3.5 t together with a light trailer, that is, one whose maximum permissible mass does not exceed 750 kg. A tractor with trailers requires category T, and a combination of 4.5 t exceeds the basic entitlement.
q-6414: Correct answer: C. The moment its validity expires, a driving licence stops entitling you to drive, and there is no transitional period. The document must be replaced before that date, otherwise driving is treated as driving without entitlement.
q-7513: Correct answer: B. The owner must indicate, at the request of an authorised body, to whom they entrusted the vehicle at a given time. They are released from this only when the vehicle was used by an unknown person against their will and knowledge and they could not have prevented it.
q-10040: Correct answer: B. The rules do not allow you to walk away from the vehicle while the engine is running — no distance is permitted here. Before walking away, switch off the engine and secure the vehicle against moving off on its own.
q-10083: Correct answer: C. A moped is by definition a vehicle with a design speed not exceeding 45 km/h, so riding at 50 km/h is not permitted regardless of whether a passenger is carried and at what time of day.
q-10087: Correct answer: C. An international driving permit is issued for a period no longer than 3 years and in no case longer than the validity of the national driving licence on the basis of which it was issued. A medical certificate does not extend that period.
q-10089: Correct answer: C. An invalid driving licence gives no entitlement to drive — from the moment it expires the driver is treated as a person without entitlement. The rules provide for no transitional period here, neither a week nor thirty days.
q-10090: Correct answer: C. The entitlement to drive an agricultural tractor on the basis of category B applies only on the territory of Poland. Abroad this extension is not recognised — there the appropriate category of driving licence is needed for a tractor.
q-10091: Correct answer: A. A driver who has held category B for at least 3 years may ride a motorcycle with an engine capacity of up to 125 cm³ and limited power. This entitlement applies in Poland and involves no additional speed limit.
q-10093: Correct answer: C. Category B allows you to drive a combination of a car and a trailer if the combined maximum permissible mass does not exceed 3.5 tonnes. This entitlement is not subject to a condition of driving at up to 30 km/h.
q-10094: Correct answer: A. An international driving permit is issued by the starosta, the same authority that issues the national driving licence, at the driver's request and on the basis of a valid national document. The voivode does not deal with these matters.
q-10108: Correct answer: B. Category B includes the entitlement to drive a moped and a light quadricycle, so a separate category AM is not needed. The entitlement is not limited to a built-up area or to the area outside it.
q-10816: Correct answer: B. A driving licence is taken away against a receipt when the driver exceeds the permitted speed by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area. Exceeding it by exactly 50 km/h, or the same excess outside a built-up area, does not result in the document being taken.
q-10819: Correct answer: A. The administrative decision to retain a driving licence is issued when the permitted speed is exceeded by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area. Outside a built-up area such an excess results in a fine and points, but not in that decision.
q-10822: Correct answer: C. For exceeding the permitted speed by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area, the driving licence is retained for 3 months. That period runs from the actual surrender of the document, and driving despite the ban extends it.
q-10829: Correct answer: A. A vehicle's admission to traffic is confirmed by the registration document, in which the result of the technical inspection is recorded. The vehicle card documents its history, and the control sticker on the window admits nothing by itself.
q-10885: Correct answer: B. Neither the registration document of a Polish vehicle nor the insurance policy needs to be carried, because the data are in the registers. You must, however, have with you the receipt for a retained registration document, as long as it entitles you to use the vehicle.
q-10886: Correct answer: B. You must have with you the receipt for a retained temporary permit for the period in which it entitles you to use the vehicle. Confirmation of voluntary insurance and a technical inspection certificate are not required while driving.
q-10887: Correct answer: B. The registration document of a Polish vehicle itself need not be carried — it is checked in the register. What is compulsory is the receipt for its retention, as long as that document entitles you to use the vehicle.
q-10888: Correct answer: A. The driver carries the receipt for a retained temporary permit as long as it replaces the document admitting the vehicle to traffic. A certificate of conformity or the registration document of a Polish vehicle need not be carried.
q-10889: Correct answer: A. A vehicle registered abroad is not visible in the Polish registers, so the driver must carry the document admitting it to traffic and show it on request. Personal accident insurance is voluntary and not required.
q-10890: Correct answer: B. With a vehicle registered abroad, the Polish services cannot check the insurance in their system, so the driver carries the document confirming compulsory third-party insurance. Proof of ownership and stamp duty are irrelevant here.
q-10891: Correct answer: B. When driving a vehicle registered abroad, you must have with you proof of payment of the compulsory third-party insurance premium. Road tolls are settled separately and are not the subject of this duty.
q-10892: Correct answer: B. A national driving licence need not be carried, because the entitlements are in the register. If, however, you drive on the basis of another document confirming entitlement, for example one issued abroad, you must have it with you.
q-10893: Correct answer: B. When a driving licence has been retained, the document entitling you to drive is the receipt, and you must have it with you for the period in which it entitles you to drive. Medical and psychological certificates are not carried by the driver.
q-10894: Correct answer: B. You must have with you the receipt for a retained driving licence for the period in which it entitles you to drive the vehicle. The psychological and medical certificates are kept outside the vehicle — they are not needed for a roadside check.
q-10895: Correct answer: B. The duty to carry applies to a document confirming entitlement to drive other than a national driving licence, because only national entitlements appear in the register. Course certificates are not required while driving.
q-10898: Correct answer: B. Carrying a number of people exceeding by two the number of seats entered in the registration document results in the driving licence being retained. The other breaches listed are punished with a fine and points, but the document itself is not taken for them.
q-10899: Correct answer: B. The driving licence is retained when the number of people carried exceeds by two the number of seats specified in the temporary permit. The other behaviours listed end in a fine and points, not in the document being taken.
q-10930: Correct answer: B. In such a case the receipt for a retained national driving licence entitles you to drive for a further 24 hours. After that time, driving on is already driving without entitlement.
q-10931: Correct answer: B. Also when the licence is retained for carrying too many people, the receipt allows you to drive the vehicle for 24 hours. After that the document must be recovered, and driving without it is driving without entitlement.
q-10960: Correct answer: C. Exceeding the speed limit by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area usually ends with the driving licence being retained, but this is not applied when the driver acted to save a person's life or health. The police officer then does not retain the document.
q-10961: Correct answer: C. Retention of the driving licence for exceeding the speed limit by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area is not applied if the driver exceeded the speed while saving a person's life or health. The police officer then refrains from retaining the document.
q-11001: Correct answer: C. The driver of a vehicle registered in Poland need not carry the registration document or proof of third-party insurance, because those data are in the registers. They must, however, have the certificate of the technical check of the alcohol interlock if their entitlement is restricted to such a vehicle.
q-11005: Correct answer: A. A registration document retained because of the vehicle's technical condition is returned by a unit authorised to carry out technical inspections, after an inspection corresponding to the reason for retention. Neither the municipal guard nor the road authority has such powers.
q-11017: Correct answer: A. For exceeding the speed limit by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area, the driving licence is retained for 3 months. That period may be extended if the driver drives a vehicle during that time despite the document being retained.
q-11018: Correct answer: A. In such a case the receipt for the retained driving licence allows you to drive for a further 24 hours from the moment the document was taken. After that time, driving on means driving without entitlement.
q-11022: Correct answer: A. The driving licence is not retained when the driver exceeded the speed while acting to avert an immediate danger to an interest protected by law. Pressure from another driver, or wanting to clear a junction faster, is no such justification.
q-14062: Correct answer: C. Driving despite a driving-licence retention extended to six months ends with the driving entitlement being withdrawn for 5 years from the day that event is established. The reason for the original retention does not change this consequence.
q-14063: Correct answer: C. Driving a vehicle during a driving-licence retention extended to six months leads to the entitlement being withdrawn for 5 years from the day that event is established. The retention period is then no longer extended further.
q-14064: Correct answer: C. The driving licence is retained against a receipt when a car is carrying 3 people more than the number of seats in the registration document. A smaller excess is punished, but does not result in the document being retained.
q-1877: Correct answer: B. The load must be arranged so as not to impair the stability of the combination — a badly placed load makes the trailer sway and causes loss of control of the vehicle. It must not cover the lights or be left unsecured either.
q-1878: Correct answer: A. The load must be secured against shifting, because under braking or on a bend it moves and changes the distribution of mass. Low speed changes nothing — the duty to secure it is unconditional.
q-1879: Correct answer: C. A loose load is carried in a sealed load compartment and covered, so that it neither spills nor blows onto the road. Material falling from under the wheels endangers motorcyclists and cyclists in particular.
q-1880: Correct answer: A. Straps and other fastening devices are secured so that they neither loosen nor fall off while driving. A loosely hanging item may catch on the road, strike another road user or release the load.
q-1881: Correct answer: C. The load must not restrict the driver's view of the road — that is a condition of controlling the vehicle. It must not cover the lights or number plates either, or hinder the use of the mirrors.
q-1882: Correct answer: A. The heaviest luggage is placed low and deep, in the middle part of the boot, because this lowers the centre of gravity and improves the car's stability. A heavy object placed high can be thrown into the cabin under braking.
q-1883: Correct answer: A. The load is arranged so that it does not cover the trailer's lights or reflectors — otherwise the driver behind will not read braking or a change of direction. The mass is also distributed evenly, not on one side.
q-1888: Correct answer: A. Towing a person on a sledge, skis or roller skates behind a vehicle is prohibited, because such a person has no protection and can fall under the wheels at any moment. A CB radio and a child seat in the front seat are allowed.
q-1905: Correct answer: C. The fire extinguisher is mounted low and within reach, for example under the passenger seat, so that it is available at once and does not turn into a projectile under harsh braking. A loose extinguisher is dangerous for the people in the car.
q-3615: Correct answer: B. A combination of a car and a trailer may travel at no more than 80 km/h on the road beyond this sign — the high limits that apply on it concern only vehicles without a trailer. A trailer lengthens the braking distance and worsens the stability of the combination.
q-4375: Correct answer: C. A carried load must not cover the lights, reflectors or the number plate, and must not restrict the driver's view. Roof-rack carriers meet these conditions, and the bicycles must be firmly fastened.
q-6355: Correct answer: B. The sign warns of a stretch where wild animals often run across the carriageway. Slow down and watch the verges and the edge of the forest, because animals move in groups and the first is usually followed by more.
q-6386: Correct answer: C. The number of people carried may not exceed the number of seats entered in the registration document. Every person, a child included, takes one seat and must wear a belt or travel in a child seat. No rule allows an extra passenger beyond that number.
q-6389: Correct answer: C. The duty to fasten seat belts also applies to the rear seats, regardless of where you are driving. In a collision an unbelted rear passenger strikes the back of the front seat with a force of many tonnes and endangers the person sitting in front.
q-6397: Correct answer: B. A child is carried in a child seat matched to its weight and height, correctly fitted to the seat. On an adult's lap, under braking or in a collision, it is crushed by that person's weight, and their belt gives it no protection at all.
q-6398: Correct answer: A. An infant may be carried only in a child seat matched to its weight and height, correctly fitted in the vehicle. No arms will hold a child under braking or in an impact, and an adult's belt then crushes it with enormous force.
q-6399: Correct answer: B. A newborn is carried in a child seat matched to its weight and height, correctly fitted in the vehicle, usually rear-facing, which best protects the head and neck. A random carrier or an adult's lap gives no such protection.
q-6402: Correct answer: A. A load may protrude at the rear by no more than 2 m beyond the rear plane of the vehicle's outline. The protruding end must be clearly marked, and in conditions of insufficient visibility additionally with a red light and a red reflector.
q-6403: Correct answer: A. A combination of a car and a trailer may be no more than 18.75 m long. Exceeding that value is not permitted, and the longer the combination, the harder it is to manoeuvre, overtake and fit round bends.
q-6406: Correct answer: A. A combination of vehicles is a motor vehicle together with a trailer coupled to it, for example a car with a trailer. A motorcycle with a sidecar is a single vehicle, and vehicles joined for towing do not form a combination in this sense.
q-6470: Correct answer: B. Choking must be dealt with immediately, because seconds count: stop the vehicle in a safe place, take the child out, tilt it head down and strike between the shoulder blades. Driving to hospital or just waiting for help loses precious time.
q-7248: Correct answer: A. The speed at this place is decided by the sign shown in the material, which raises the limit applying in the built-up area, so driving at 70 km/h in a vehicle with a maximum permissible mass of 2.5 t is allowed. The time of day is irrelevant here.
q-7249: Correct answer: B. On a single-carriageway expressway a car may travel at no more than 100 km/h. The speed of 120 km/h applies to a dual-carriageway expressway, and 90 km/h to other roads outside a built-up area.
q-7445: Correct answer: C. Towing behind a vehicle a person on a sledge, skis, roller skates or a similar device is prohibited. Towing a light trailer and towing another car are — once the conditions are met — allowed.
q-7451: Correct answer: C. A load protruding from the rear of the vehicle is marked with a red flag. In conditions of insufficient visibility, a red light and a reflector are used instead of the flag.
q-7452: Correct answer: B. The actual total mass of a trailer towed by a car may not exceed the actual total mass of that car. The restriction protects the stability of the combination and the effectiveness of braking.
q-7454: Correct answer: A. On a motorway towing another vehicle is prohibited — an immobilised vehicle may only be brought to the nearest exit. On an expressway and in a residential zone towing remains allowed under the general rules.
q-7455: Correct answer: A. When towing another vehicle, a speed of up to 30 km/h applies in a built-up area and up to 60 km/h outside it. This limit is binding even when the general limit on the stretch is higher.
q-7512: Correct answer: B. A towed car is marked with a reflective warning triangle placed at the rear on the left side. Switching on the hazard lights or the rear fog light does not replace this marking.
q-7780: Correct answer: B. When towing another vehicle outside a built-up area, speed may not exceed 60 km/h — and that is exactly the stretch of road the signs in the material define. In a built-up area a lower limit applies to towing.
q-10067: Correct answer: C. A towed vehicle blocks the view in the rear-view mirror and makes it harder to judge what is happening behind. The driver must then use the exterior mirrors more often, drive more slowly and leave more room for manoeuvres.
q-10081: Correct answer: A. A vehicle with a faulty steering system may not be towed, because even with a rigid coupling the driver of the towed vehicle has to steer it. Such a vehicle is carried on a flatbed or with the axle raised, so that steering is not needed.
q-10084: Correct answer: B. The permitted length of a combination consisting of a car and a trailer is 18.75 metres. It is measured for the whole combination including the coupling device, and the fact that the trailer is a caravan changes nothing.
q-10085: Correct answer: A. A load on a trailer must always be fastened so that it does not shift under acceleration, braking and on bends. No speed releases you from this duty — a shifted load changes the distribution of mass and can make the trailer sway.
q-10086: Correct answer: C. The load is arranged so as not to impair the stability of the combination — placed too high or unevenly, it makes the trailer sway. Apart from that it must be fastened and must not cover the lights or the number plate.
q-10095: Correct answer: A. The permitted number of people carried is entered in the vehicle's registration document, alongside other technical data. It may not be exceeded, even if there is physically enough room in the cabin.
q-10109: Correct answer: B. Only a vehicle with working braking and steering systems may be towed, because the rider of a towed motorcycle must be able to stop it. The requirement applies at any speed, not only above 20 km/h.
q-10806: Correct answer: C. A rear-facing child seat may be placed on the front seat only when the passenger airbag is switched off. An inflating airbag would strike the back of the child seat, that is, the child's head, with enormous force.
